text.p: Alexandre Lamfalussy, head of the European Monetary Institute said on Monday evening that it would be no problem for the future European Central Bank to pursue a decentralised currency market intervention policy.

Speaking to reporters at Frankfurt's International Business Journalists' Forum, Lamfalussy said that there was no reason for intervention to take place centrally, providing the orders to intervene were given by the ECB directly.
"The decision to intervene is a central decision, a control mechanism on a real-time basis," he said. "Experience in exchange markets shows that it does not really matter who does it (intervenes)."
Funding for these operations could be provided either by the national central banks acting as an agent for the ECB, or by their holding a proportion of ECB reserves.

A recent report published by the EMI left open the question of whether or not the European System of Central Banks would intervene in foreign exchange markets on a centralised or decentralised basis. But it made clear that only the 50 billion ECU or so in funds the ECB will hold in reserves could be used for this.
